section#s3.sec
  ## 3 Findings
  article#dimm-CPU0_C1.card.g-replace
    ### CPU0_C1 DDR5 RDIMM 64 GB 2Rx4 Example Memory EXM64G48R2X4-A S/N BE8ED6
    finding = replace now R-UE-01 4 uncorrected errors, the latest on 2026-11-12 10:10 UTC at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f col 0x238 4 records
    evidence = R-LOOP-01 uncorrected errors at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f col 0x238 in 4 of the last 8 boots: each of these boots ended in a fatal hardware error 64 records supports the other 15 DIMMs of this host have no unconfined errors: a cause in the board is unlikely supports no other DIMM of the host had an uncorrected error in these boots
    next = Replace the DIMM. Attach a case bundle written from the kept ledger to the return.
    p.sub: confidence high, 1 more statement, 2 checks not made, 2 kinds of data missing: the whole finding
    p.links: topology and address map timeline checks
  article#dimm-CPU1_D1.card.g-observe
    ### CPU1_D1 DDR5 RDIMM 64 GB 2Rx4 Example Memory EXM64G48R2X4-A S/N 21FD6F
    finding = observe R-SOFT-01 one cell fails repeatedly (rank1 dev10 bg3 bank2 row 0xbce2 col 0x4c8): 25 errors since 2026-08-05, 4 in the last 7 days 25 records
    evidence = R-SOFT-01 the fault at rank1 dev10 bg3 bank2 row 0xbce2 col 0x4c8 had errors in 3 of the last 8 boots
    next = No action. Look again when the count grows or a new place appears.
    p.sub: confidence medium: the whole finding
    p.links: topology and address map timeline checks
  p.how: The finding line gives the grade, the rule that set it and what that rule saw. Below stand at most three statements that bear on the decision: what the other rules saw, and checks that speak for the finding ("supports") or against it ("weakens"). A count of records leads to the records. The last line gives the confidence and counts what the whole finding in the appendix adds: further statements, checks that could not be made, missing data.
  ### Rules named in this report
  table.rules
    | rule | grade it gives | fires when
    | R-UE-01 | replace now | an uncorrected error on this DIMM
    | R-LOOP-01 | replace now | uncorrected errors at one place of the DIMM in several boots
    | R-SOFT-01 | observe | corrected errors without a growing fault: stray errors at places that did not fail again, or a fault that is neither rising nor spreading

  p.how: Each bar splits all errors of the DIMM at one level of its memory: rank, device, bank, row. A segment lies below the segment it belongs to, so the widest path from top to bottom is where the errors are.
  p.how: One bank of one device: rows down, columns across. The shade of a cell is the number of errors in it. A horizontal line is a row fault, a vertical line a column fault, one cell that repeats a single-bit fault, and a cloud over the bank a bank fault. A cell with errors leads to its records.

section#s6.sec
  ## 6 Checks against a wrong diagnosis
  p.how: Each finding was tested against causes outside the DIMM: the slot, the channel, the board, and slot names that disagree between sources. "supports" speaks for the finding and "weakens" against it. An open check could not be made from the records; where a person can settle it, the test is listed below the checks.
  section#check-dimm-CPU0_C1.dimm
    ### CPU0_C1 replace now
    #### Checks made from the records
    table.checks
      | result | check
      | open | no other DIMM on this channel: there is nothing to compare with
      | open | no slot move or reseat on record: a cause in the board is not ruled out
      | supports | the other 15 DIMMs of this host have no unconfined errors: a cause in the board is unlikely
      | supports | no other DIMM of the host had an uncorrected error in these boots
      | supports | the uncorrected errors stay at one place of the DIMM: a fault of a contact or a trace corrupts whatever address is read
    #### Tests for a person
    li: Swap the DIMM with one from another channel, or reseat it, and scan again after some days. The ledger then shows whether the errors follow the DIMM, stay in the slot or stop.
  section#check-dimm-CPU1_D1.dimm
    ### CPU1_D1 observe
    #### Checks made from the records
    p: The records gave no check for this finding.
    #### Tests for a person
    p: No test is open.

section#s8.sec
  ## 8 Appendix
  ### About this case
  Case ID = 0123456789ab the first 12 digits of the identity of the ledger
  Host = synth-crash-loop
  Collected = synthetic data set, 2026-11-13 00:00 UTC
  Report = customer report, generated 2026-11-13 09:30 UTC by my test
  Engine = version 8
  p.how: A grade is a finding. The thresholds behind it are defaults that have not been compared with failure analysis results.
  ### Findings in full
  article#full-dimm-CPU0_C1.card.g-replace
    #### CPU0_C1 DDR5 RDIMM 64 GB 2Rx4 Example Memory EXM64G48R2X4-A S/N BE8ED6
    finding = replace now (finding, confidence high) R-UE-01 R-LOOP-01
    evidence = R-UE-01 4 uncorrected errors, the latest on 2026-11-12 10:10 UTC at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f col 0x238 4 records R-LOOP-01 uncorrected errors at rank0 dev7 bg0 bank3 row 0x1a2f col 0x238 in 4 of the last 8 boots: each of these boots ended in a fatal hardware error 64 records
    checks = open no other DIMM on this channel: there is nothing to compare with open no slot move or reseat on record: a cause in the board is not ruled out supports the other 15 DIMMs of this host have no unconfined errors: a cause in the board is unlikely supports no other DIMM of the host had an uncorrected error in these boots supports the uncorrected errors stay at one place of the DIMM: a fault of a contact or a trace corrupts whatever address is read
    missing = no ECS counters no DIMM temperature history
    baseline = own history: 3.3 errors a day over the last 7 days, percentile 93 of the 30 days before same part number (EXM64G48R2X4-A): percentile 97 among the 16 DIMMs in this ledger, 2 of them with errors
    next = Replace the DIMM. Attach a case bundle written from the kept ledger to the return.
  article#full-dimm-CPU1_D1.card.g-observe
    #### CPU1_D1 DDR5 RDIMM 64 GB 2Rx4 Example Memory EXM64G48R2X4-A S/N 21FD6F
